{{also|Love|LoVe|løve|lové|lóve|lóvé|lőve|лове}} {{minitoc}} ==English== [[File:Frank Bernard Dicksee - Romeo and Juliet, 1884.jpg|thumb|Romeo and Juliet in love|alt=A painting of a kiss on a balcony]] [[File:Heart corazón.svg|thumb|The heart symbol, a popular symbol of love|alt=Heart symbol]] {{wikipedia}} {{wikidata lexeme|L1029}} {{wikidata lexeme|L4471}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|loue||obsolete}} * {{alt|en|luv||Internet slang|or|texting}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/lʌv/|[lʌv]|a=RP,GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-love.ogg|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-love.wav|a=Southern England}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-love.ogg|a=GA}} * {{IPA|en|/lɐv/|[lä̝v]|~|[lɐ̞v]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/lʊv/|[lʊv]|a=Northern England,Ireland,non-foot-strut split}} * {{IPA|en|/ləʋ/|[lɐʊ̯]|[lɐʋ]|a=India}} * {{rhymes|en|ʌv|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|love}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|id=love}} {{ety|en|:inh|enm:love|id=affection|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|love}}, {{m|enm|luve}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lufu}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*lubu}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*lubō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewbʰ-|t=love, care, desire}}. The ''close of a letter'' sense is presumably a truncation of ''With love'' or the like. Hidden|title=Jewish, Christian, and Islamic Mystical Perspectives on the '''Love''' of God|isbn=1137443324}} ## [[affectionate|Affectionate]], [[benevolent]] [[concern]] or [[care]] for other [[people]] or [[being]]s, and for their [[well-being]]. ##* '''1864''', ''Utilitarianism Explained and Exemplified in Moral and Political Government'': ##*: The '''love''' of your neighbor as yourself, is expressly given as the definition and test of Charity,—not alms-giving—and this '''love''' is [...] the highest of all the Divine commands[.] ##* {{quote-book |en |year=1963 |author=[[w:Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King, Jr.]] |chapter=A Tough Mind and a Tender Heart |title=w:Strength to Love |url=https://archive.org/details/strengthtolove00king/ |location=[[New York]] |publisher=w:Pocket Books |year_published=1964 |OCLC=768659813 |page=7 |pageurl=https://archive.org/details/strengthtolove00king/page/7/ |text=Through nonviolent resistance we shall be able to oppose the unjust system and at the same time '''love''' the perpetrators of the system. We must work passionately and unrelentingly for full stature as citizens, but may it never be said, my friends, that to gain it we used the inferior methods of falsehood, malice, hate, and violence.}} ## A [[feeling]] of [[intense]] [[attraction]] towards someone. ##: {{ux|en|I have never been in '''love''' as much as I have with you.}} ##* {{RQ:Congreve Mourning Bride|page=39|passage=Heav'n has no Rage, like '''Love''' to Hatred turn'd, / Nor Hell a Fury, like a Woman ſcorn'd.}} ##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her '''love''' for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}} ## A deep or [[abiding]] [[liking]] for something; an [[enthusiasm]] for something. ##: {{ux|en|My '''love''' of cricket knows no bounds.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Philip Auerswald|title=The Coming Prosperity|isbn=0199930848 |passage=For three decades, the average number of miles driven by US motorists increased steadily. Then, in 2007, that steady climb was suddenly halted. [...] What magic caused Americans to temper their longstanding '''love''' of the open road?}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A person who is the object of [[romantic]] feelings; a [[darling]], a [[sweetheart]], a [[beloved]]. #: {{syn|en|baby|darling|honey|lover|pet|sweetheart|Thesaurus:sweetheart}} #* {{quote-text|en|year=1595|author=w:Edmund Spenser|title=s:Epithalamion |passage=Open the temple gates unto my '''love'''.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|III|2|text=O '''love''', dispatch all business, and be gone!}} #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage='Oh, my '''love''', my '''love'''!' she murmured, 'wilt thou ever know how I have loved thee?' and she kissed him on the forehead, and then went and stood in the pathway of the flame of Life.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1969|author=The Dubliners|title=Dirty Old Town|passage=I met my '''love''' by the gasworks wall.}} # {{lb|en|colloquial|Commonwealth}} {{non-gloss|A term of friendly address, regardless of feelings.}} #: {{syn|en|mate|darling|lovey|sweetie|sweetheart}} #: {{ux|en|Hello '''love''', how can I help you?}} # A thing, activity{{,}} etc. which is the object of one's deep liking or [[enthusiasm]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1997|month=March|title=Faces of Today's Black Woman|journal=Ebony|volume=52|issue=5|page=96 |passage=But it wasn't until [Theresa M.   I '''love''' that song!}} #* {{RQ:Burroughs Land That Time Forgot||VI|passage= wanted to take her in my arms and tell her how I '''loved''' her, and had taken her hand from the rail and started to draw her toward me when Olson came blundering up on deck with his bedding.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=February 26 2013|author={{w|Pink (singer)|Pink}}; w:Nate Ruess|journal=w:Just Give Me a Reason |passage=Just give me a reason, / just a little bit's enough, / just a second we're not broken, just bent / and we can learn to '''love''' again.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To need, [[thrive]] on. #: {{ux|en|Mold '''loves''' moist, dark places.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To be strongly inclined towards something; an emphatic form of ''[[like]]''. #: {{ux|en|I '''love''' walking barefoot on wet grass;  I'd '''love''' to join the team;  I '''love''' what you've done with your hair}} #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage="I '''love''' not that underlings should perceive my wisdom."}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1920|author=Agatha Christie|authorlink=Agatha Christie|title={{w|The Mysterious Affair at Styles}}|publisher=Pan Books|location=London|year_published=1954|page=141|passage=“Everywhere he went, I went with him. 3=== {{ety|en|:uder|fr:œuf|id=zero|tree=1}} Now widely believed (due to historical written record) to be from the idea that when one does a thing “for love” it is for no monetary gain, the word “love” thus implying “nothing”. Use of “love” for having no score extends to the 18th century in tennis as well as certain card games.{{cite-web |en-US |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/06/04/nx-s1-5843257/tennis-love-french-open |title=How having zero points in tennis — or 'love' — came to sound so sweet |first=Anya |last=Archie |date=2026-06-04 |publisher={{w|NPR}} |work=Word of the week|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261003092755/https://www.npr.org/2026/06/04/nx-s1-5843257/tennis-love-french-open|archivedate=3 October 2026}} The former assumption that it had originated from French {{m|fr|œuf|l’œuf|lit=the egg}}, due to its shape, has largely been discredited and is no longer widely accepted. However, the apparent similarity of the shape of an egg to a zero has inspired similar analogies, such as the use of {{m|en|duck}} (reputed to be short for duck's egg) for a zero score at cricket, and {{m|en|goose egg}} for "zero". ====Noun==== {{en-noun|-}} # {{lb|en|racquet sports|billiards}} [[zero|Zero]], no score. #: {{ux|en|So that’s fifteen-'''love''' to Kournikova.}} #* {{quote-text|en|year=2013|author=w:Paul McNamee|title=Game Changer: My Tennis Life |passage=The next day [[w:Andre Agassi|Agassi]] came back from two sets to '''love''' down to beat Courier in five sets.}} # Nothing; no recompense. #* {{quote-text|en|year=1916|author=H.
